item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: A ruler measuring the length of a pipe]

What is the length of the pipe being measured?
item.figure_description: A horizontal ruler labeled "Meters (m)" at the top has major tick marks from 0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.1, with minor tick marks halfway between each major tick mark (representing increments of 0.05). Below the ruler, a gray cylindrical pipe is positioned horizontally. Dimension lines with arrows indicate the length being measured from the left end of the pipe, which aligns with 0 on the ruler, to the right end of the pipe, which aligns with the tick mark halfway between 0.8 and 0.9.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Ruler]

Using a centimeter ruler like this one, you can measure accurately to the nearest
reference_items.figure_description: A centimeter ruler labeled "cm" at the left, with major tick marks numbered from 1 to 11. Between each pair of consecutive whole-centimeter marks (and between 0 and 1), there is exactly one intermediate, unnumbered tick mark of medium length indicating each half-centimeter. There are no smaller millimeter subdivision marks.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A ruler with a wavy string above it]

If the string in the diagram is pulled straight, which of these is closest to its length?
reference_items.figure_description: A metric ruler marked from 0 to 11 cm, with ticks at every centimeter and half-centimeter, labeled 'cm' at the left end and with numbers 1 through 11. Above the ruler, a curved line labeled 'string' begins at the 3 cm mark, extends horizontally to approximately 5.5 cm, loops back leftward to about 4.7 cm, and then extends horizontally rightward, ending near the 7 cm mark.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Two horizontal pipes]

The first pipe is x meters long. The second pipe is y times as long as the first one. How long is the second pipe?
reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal cylindrical pipes arranged end-to-end horizontally. The first pipe on the left is shorter, with a rounded left end, an oval opening at the right end, and the label "x meters" inside. The second pipe on the right is longer, with a rounded left end, an oval opening at the right end, and no label.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Front of a building with a car parked outside]

The car is 3.5 m long. About how long is the building?
reference_items.figure_description: A line drawing showing the front facade of a single-story building. In the center is a double door with an arched window above it. Symmetrically flanking the doors are six identical rectangular windows with multipaned sashes: three windows to the left of the door and three to the right. Parked on the ground along the far left of the building facade is a black car, positioned spanning the space of roughly the first two windows. The length of the entire building is approximately four times the length of the car.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A rectangular shaped swimming pool has a paved walkway around it as shown.

[Image: Diagram of a pool and walkway]

What is the area of the paved walkway?
reference_items.figure_description: A diagram shows an outer shaded rectangle labeled "Walkway" surrounding an unshaded inner rectangle labeled "Pool". The dimensions of the outer rectangle are labeled with double-headed arrows: a length of 70 m along the top and a width of 23 m along the right side. The dimensions of the inner rectangle are also labeled with double-headed arrows: a length of 50 m along its top edge and a width of 18 m along its right edge.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Number line from 0 to 3 with a point P marked]

What is the best estimate of the number corresponding to P?
reference_items.figure_description: A horizontal number line with an arrow pointing right. Four evenly spaced vertical tick marks are labeled below with the numbers 0, 1, 2, and 3. On the line between 1 and 2, slightly to the right of 1 (at approximately one-fifth of the distance from 1 to 2), there is a solid black point labeled "P" directly above it.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
